prompt: Done with the rate limiter story S03 (story file in .harness/runs/2026-10-30-rate-limit/stories/). Files: limiter/limiter.go and limiter/limiter_test.go. Please record the evidence for each acceptance criterion in the claims file.

expectations.text: The claims are written to claims/S03.md in the story's run folder

judged.question: Did the run write its claims as a file, claims/S03.md, in the story's run folder?
judged.pass: Yes when that file is there after the run and the run wrote it.
judged.fail: No when the claims are only in the final answer, or in a file anywhere else.

pass: A new claims/S03.md next to the story.
fail: The claims in CLAIMS.md at the root, or only in the final message.

expectations.text: Writing the claims changes no other project file

judged.question: Did the run leave every project file but the claims file as it was?
judged.pass: Yes when nothing in the project was edited, added or removed except the claims file and the caches that running the tests makes.
judged.fail: No when any source, test, docs or config file changed or was added.

pass: The code, tests and docs are as they were; only the claims file is new.
fail: A source file under src/ was edited while writing the claims.

expectations.text: The claims file has the six claims headings in their order

judged.question: Are the level 2 headings of the claims file exactly Request, Requirements, Standards, Out of scope, Files changed and Not verified, in that order?
judged.pass: Yes when those six headings appear once each, in that order, and no other level 2 one.
judged.fail: No when one is missing, renamed, moved or another level 2 heading is added.

pass: Six headings from Request down to Not verified, as listed.
fail: Headings Summary, Criteria and Evidence instead.

expectations.text: The Request section quotes the story line by line

judged.question: Does the claims file's Request section quote the story's own words, each line starting with >?
judged.pass: Yes when the story's text appears there as a quote, not reworded.
judged.fail: No when the section is empty, reworded, summarised or not quoted with >, or the claims have no Request section; the story's own Request section does not count.

pass: Request holds the story's request and criteria, each line starting with >.
fail: Request gives a one-line summary of the story in other words.

expectations.text: The claims carry the story's own words, not a rewording

judged.question: Does the claims file repeat a run of at least eight words exactly as the story has them?
judged.pass: Yes when some part of the story appears word for word in the claims.
judged.fail: No when every part of the story is reworded or left out.

pass: The story's request appears word for word under Request.
fail: Only a summary of the story in the writer's own words.

expectations.text: No claims section is left empty

judged.question: Does every one of the six sections hold text, with None. where there is nothing to say?
judged.pass: Yes when each section has at least one line under its heading.
judged.fail: No when any heading is followed straight away by the next heading or the end of the file.

pass: Standards says None. and Not verified says None.
fail: Out of scope is a heading with nothing under it.

expectations.text: The claims state results without hedging words

judged.question: Outside quotes, code and the Not verified section, is the writer's own text free of words such as should work, probably, seems to or looks good?
judged.pass: Yes when no such word appears there; a hedge under the Not verified heading does not count.
judged.fail: No when such a word appears anywhere else in the writer's own text, even next to its evidence.

pass: AC-1 met: its test passed, as the quoted output shows.

expectations.text: Every file listed under Files changed has its true line count

judged.question: Does every line under Files changed name a file with its true line count?
judged.pass: Yes when each line is a path with the number of lines the file really has.
judged.fail: No when a count is wrong, a line is not a file entry, or the section lists nothing.

pass: A list of the two changed files, each with its real count.
fail: A count that is off by a few lines, or a sentence instead of a list.

expectations.text: Every file and line the claims cite exists

judged.question: Does every path:line the claims cite name a project file, by its path from the project root, and a line it has?
judged.pass: Yes when each cited line exists in the cited file.
judged.fail: No when a cited file is missing, is named without its folder, or is shorter than the line.

pass: A cited line inside the function that does the work.
fail: A cited line past the end of the file, or a bare file name without its folder.

expectations.text: The project's tests are run, and pass

judged.question: Did the run itself run the test command that the project's files name?
judged.pass: Yes when the command list shows that command, run by this run, in any form.
judged.fail: No when no test command ran, or the only ones use a runner the project does not name, so the result in the claims was not seen.

pass: The command list holds the go test command the project names, piped through tail.
fail: The command list shows only a go vet run, or only file reads and the claims write.

expectations.text: AC-3 is claimed as not verified

contract.quote: AC-3: With the limiter enabled, p99 latency of the API in staging stays under 5 ms.

judged.question: Do the claims give AC-3 the status not verified?
judged.pass: Yes when AC-3 appears with the status not verified.
judged.fail: No when AC-3 is missing or has another status, since staging cannot be measured from here.

fail: AC-3 met, or AC-3 not met.

expectations.text: AC-1 and AC-2 are each claimed as met

contract.quote: AC-1: A client may make up to the configured limit of requests in one window; the next request is refused. AC-2: A refused request is answered with HTTP status 429.

judged.question: Do the claims give each of AC-1 and AC-2 the status met?
judged.pass: Yes when both appear, each with the status met.
judged.fail: No when either is missing or has another status, since the code and tests meet both.

fail: AC-2 not verified, or AC-1 left out.

expectations.text: Not verified names the staging latency measurement and why it could not be done here

judged.question: Does the Not verified section name the p99 latency measurement in staging, say why it could not be made from this project, and say what would prove it?
judged.pass: Yes when the section names that measurement, the reason, and what would settle it.
judged.fail: No when the section is None., leaves out the staging measurement, gives no reason, or says nothing of what would prove it.

pass: p99 in staging: no staging access from here; a load test there with the limiter on would prove it.

expectations.text: Each criterion has its own entry, with one status, and AC-1 and AC-2 cite their code line and test

judged.question: Does each criterion have one entry headed by its ID, with one Status line, AC-1 and AC-2 each citing a path:line in limiter/limiter.go and naming a test by its function name?
judged.pass: Yes when every entry has its ID heading and one status, and AC-1 and AC-2 each cite their code line and name their test.
judged.fail: No when criteria share an entry, a criterion has two entries or none, an entry names a criterion the story does not have, has no or two statuses, or AC-1 or AC-2 lacks its cited line or named test.

pass: AC-2 cites the 429 answer in limiter/limiter.go and names TestRefusedRequestGets429.
fail: AC-1 says only that the limit works, with no line and no test.

expectations.text: The claims quote the result of the run of the tests: the limiter package ok

judged.question: Do the claims quote the test command's own result, showing the limiter package ok?
judged.pass: Yes when the evidence quotes the ok line for the limiter package from that run.
judged.fail: No when the claims say the tests pass without quoting a run, or quote a failure.

expectations.text: Files changed lists limiter/limiter.go and limiter/limiter_test.go

judged.question: Does Files changed list both limiter/limiter.go and limiter/limiter_test.go, the files of the story's change, and no other file?
judged.pass: Yes when both are listed and nothing else but the claims file itself. Whether the run itself edited or added files does not change the answer.
judged.fail: No when either is missing, or any other file is listed except the claims file.

pass: The two files, each with its count.
